2610.05197.title: From Scientific Observations to Mechanisms: Benchmarking Hypothesis Generation by AI Scientists
2610.05197.paper_summary: Data-driven mechanistic hypotheses are essential to scientific discovery because they explain how underlying processes produce observed phenomena. AI agents and AI scientists increasingly support scientific data analysis. However, their ability to turn empirical findings into mechanistic hypotheses remains insufficiently examined. To address this gap, we introduce MechHypoBench, the first benchmark for evaluating whether AI agents and AI scientists can generate such hypotheses from empirical data. It combines paper-derived mechanisms from 14 scientific fields with real-world datasets containing 17.98 million records. The construction retains the observational complexity of empirical data while providing a specified underlying mechanism. Agents analyze the observations and propose open-form hypotheses. We develop an evaluation framework that assesses open-form mechanistic hypotheses through their consequences under withheld conditions. Experiments with general agents and AI scientists reveal a substantial gap between generated hypotheses and the underlying mechanisms.
2610.05197.paper_summary_zh: 數據驅動的機制假說對於科學發現至關重要，因為它們解釋了潛在過程如何產生觀察到的現象。AI代理和AI科學家越來越多地支持科學數據分析。 然而，它們將實證發現轉化為機制假說的能力仍然不足以進行檢驗。 為了解決這一空白，我們介紹了MechHypoBench，這是第一個評估AI代理和AI科學家是否能夠從實證數據生成此類假說的基準。 它結合了來自14個科學領域的論文衍生機制和包含1798萬條記錄的現實世界數據集。 這一構建保留了實證數據的觀察複雜性，同時提供了一個特定的潛在機制。 代理分析觀察結果並提出開放形式的假說。 我們開發了一個評估框架，通過在保留條件下的後果來評估開放形式的機制假說。 對一般代理和AI科學家的實驗顯示，生成的假說與潛在機制之間存在顯著差距。
